steps.name: Openings
steps.ask: Which task does this opening come from?

steps.name: Endings
steps.ask: Which task does this ending come from?

steps.name: Exam questions
steps.ask: Which task is this question asking for?

steps.name: Body lines
steps.ask: Review or report? Listen for the voice.

items.text: [[It is widely recognised that]] technology has transformed modern communication completely.
items.why: it states the topic in an impersonal way: no “I”, no “you”.

items.text: [[Which piece of technology would our lives be better without?]] It’s a provocative question in a world where we carry our phones [[like a second heartbeat]].
items.why: it asks the reader a question and paints a vivid picture.

items.text: [[In recent years]], social media addiction has become a significant concern among young people. [[It is widely recognised that]] excessive use has led to serious consequences for mental health.
items.why: it introduces an issue calmly and formally, as a discussion.

items.text: [[Why do so many students find it so difficult to stay healthy?]]
items.why: a question hooks the reader before any answer is given.

items.text: Nowadays, there is considerable debate about whether life today is better than in the past. [[Hence, I would like to present my views on this issue.]]
items.why: it promises a view on a debate. In an essay “I” is only for your opinion.

items.text: [[Who has never experienced a change that turned their world upside down?]]
items.why: a question every reader answers “me!”: an article pulls the reader in.

items.text: [[It is common knowledge that]] taking time off from education can have [[both positive and negative effects]].
items.why: “both positive and negative effects”: an essay promises a balanced discussion.

items.text: [[For me, the answer has always been the same:]] Sintra, a small town tucked into the hills just outside Lisbon.
items.why: “For me”: an article is personal and sounds like a person talking.

items.text: [[I visited]] last weekend to celebrate my birthday, and [[I have to say]] it exceeded all my expectations.
items.why: the writer was there: a review starts from personal experience.

items.text: [[The main objective of this report is to]] assess the school cafeteria and suggest improvements.
items.why: it states its aim in the first line, as every report does.

items.text: [[I spent a week there last summer]], and [[I have to say]] it was a brilliant experience from start to finish.
items.why: first person and enthusiasm: the writer tried it and loved it.

items.text: [[This report is based on feedback collected from students]] who regularly use the library.
items.why: it says where its information comes from: other people’s views, not the writer’s.

items.text: I downloaded it expecting to play for an hour, and [[I have to say I am still playing it three months later]].
items.why: a personal story with a smile: a review entertains as it judges.

items.text: [[This report is based on a questionnaire conducted among over 200 students.]]
items.why: a questionnaire and 200 students: a report collects facts.

items.text: [[All things considered]], it enhances communication [[when used responsibly alongside]] real-world interaction.
items.why: it weighs both sides and reaches a balanced verdict.

items.text: [[To sum up]], [[I believe]] pollution can be addressed effectively through determined action.
items.why: a formal linker to sum up, then a clear opinion: the essay’s “I” is for its view.

items.text: [[On the whole]], the best choice depends entirely on individual priorities, personality and circumstances.
items.why: it weighs the question up and concludes: no “you”, no story.

items.text: [[Whether you agree or not]], there’s no denying that some technologies leave a more complicated impression than their creators ever intended — and [[maybe it’s time we decided who is really in control]].
items.why: it talks to “you” and leaves the reader with a thought.

items.text: [[Whether you love change or not]], there’s no denying that it leaves a lasting impression on who we become — and sometimes [[the biggest disruptions turn out to be the greatest gifts]].
items.why: it ends on a memorable line for the reader to take away.

items.text: [[Whether you start with sleep, food, or movement]], there’s no denying that small, consistent steps leave a lasting impression on [[how you feel]].
items.why: friendly advice aimed straight at “you”, the reader.

items.text: [[I would highly recommend]] Bella Napoli [[to anyone interested in]] genuine Italian food.
items.why: it tells readers whether to go: every review ends with a recommendation.

items.text: [[I can assure you that]] this game will leave a lasting impression and provide hundreds of hours of genuine enjoyment.
items.why: a personal promise to the reader about something the writer has tried.

items.text: [[I would highly recommend]] The Intern [[to anyone looking for]] a film that is funny, warm and actually has something to say.
items.why: it recommends a film to a type of reader.

items.text: [[Taking everything into account, it seems clear that]] these changes would improve student satisfaction and make lunchtime more enjoyable.
items.why: an impersonal verdict on “these changes”: a report sums up its recommendations.

items.text: [[One key recommendation would be to]] introduce staggered lunch times to reduce queues.
items.why: a polite, formal suggestion to the people in charge.

items.text: [[In order to]] maximise study space, [[I would strongly recommend]] adding more library seating.
items.why: reports can say “I recommend” too, but this advice is for the people in charge (more seating), not for readers.

items.text: [[Taking everything into account, it seems clear that]] the programme [[should be offered again next year]] as it provides invaluable learning experiences.
items.why: “should be offered again”: the report advises the people who decide.

items.text: [[By far the best feature is]] the homemade pasta — [[I ordered]] the seafood linguine and it was absolutely delicious.
items.why: “I ordered”: the writer judges by their own experience.

items.text: [[The thing that is most likely to impress you is]] how he builds complex songs layer by layer [[right in front of your eyes]].
items.why: it talks to “you” and gets excited about it.

items.text: By far one of the most useful ideas was habit stacking, which [[helped me]] build a consistent study schedule.
items.why: “helped me”: a review judges by what it did for the writer.

items.text: By far the best feature is the honest recommendations — the writers are not afraid to [[tell you]] which attractions are overrated.
items.why: it speaks to “you”, the reader who might buy the guidebook.

items.text: [[The thing that is most likely to impress you is]] how it turns what could feel like a chore into something [[you actually look forward to]].
items.why: a lively “you” and a personal verdict.

items.text: However, [[one major concern expressed by students]] is the long queues at lunchtime.
items.why: the views are other people’s, reported calmly: “expressed by students”.

items.text: [[It was generally felt that]] host families were welcoming and provided comfortable accommodation.
items.why: “It was generally felt”: a report gives what the group thought, not “I”.

items.text: [[Many participants reported]] improved confidence, greater independence and a better understanding of Spanish culture.
items.why: it reports findings from many people.

items.text: By far the worst aspect of the service is the early closing time, which [[prevents many students from]] studying after school.
items.why: “By far the worst” could be a review, but the effect is on “many students”: a finding.

items.text: However, [[a common complaint relates to]] the course materials, which [[some students found]] repetitive.
items.why: a complaint gathered from others, in neutral words.

items.text: In your English class you have been talking about life in the past. Now, [[your English teacher has asked you]] to write ▁▁▁. 'Life is better today than it was 100 years ago.' [[Do you agree?]] Notes — write about: health, entertainment, …… [[(your own idea)]].
items.why: a teacher, a statement to agree with and three notes, one your own: always the essay.

items.text: In your English class you have been talking about relationships. Now, [[your English teacher has asked you]] to write ▁▁▁. Which is more important – friends or family? Notes — write about: who you can enjoy yourself with, who will help you when you have problems, …… [[(your own idea)]].
items.why: a question to discuss in class, with notes to cover: the essay.

items.text: You see this announcement in an [[English-language magazine]]. ▁▁▁ wanted! Which piece of technology would our lives be better without? [[Why?]] The best ▁▁▁ [[will be printed next month]].
items.why: a magazine asks readers for their view, and the best ones are printed: an article.

items.text: You see this announcement in an English-language magazine. ▁▁▁ wanted! [[If you could be famous for something]], what would you like to be famous for? Why? The best ▁▁▁ [[will be printed next month]].
items.why: a “what if” question for magazine readers: an article, told in your own voice.

items.text: You see this announcement in an English-language magazine. ▁▁▁ wanted! Some people love changes, others dislike them. [[What about you?]] Which changes in your life have had a big effect on you? The best ▁▁▁ [[will be printed next month]].
items.why: “What about you?”: a magazine wants personal pieces to print.

items.text: You recently saw this notice on an English-language website called TV Gold. ▁▁▁ wanted: A TV documentary I learnt a lot from. Have you seen an interesting TV documentary recently that you learnt a lot from? Write us ▁▁▁ of the documentary. You should explain what the documentary was about, tell us what you learnt from it and [[say whether other people would find it interesting too]].
items.why: something you watched, and whether others would like it: a review.

items.text: You see this announcement on an English-language technology website. ▁▁▁ wanted! Useful smartphone apps. We're looking for ▁▁▁ of smartphone apps that you find really useful. Write ▁▁▁ describing what the app does, explaining why you find it useful and saying [[whether you would recommend it to other people]].
items.why: an app you use, judged for other users: a review.

items.text: You recently saw this notice in a magazine. ▁▁▁ wanted! Useful books. Write us ▁▁▁ of a useful book which you have read. In your ▁▁▁ describe what the book is about, explain how it was useful to you and [[say why you would recommend it to others]].
items.why: a book you have read, recommended to readers: a review.

items.text: You are a member of the Student Council. [[Your school principal has asked you]] to write ▁▁▁ assessing the current school facilities and [[suggesting improvements]].
items.why: the principal wants facts and suggestions: a report.

items.text: Write ▁▁▁ [[for your school]] about the exchange programme, describing what you learned and [[whether the school should continue it]].
items.why: the school must decide whether to continue: a report helps people in charge decide.

items.text: [[The school wants to improve]] cafeteria services. Write ▁▁▁ assessing the cafeteria and [[suggesting improvements]].
items.why: the school wants to improve a service: a report assesses it and suggests changes.
